To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the polymerase domain from mouse DNA polymerase μ is the first family X enzyme to be crystallized with gapped DNA and that the structure of Pol μ with a correct dATP substrate reveals substrate interactions that differ from those of other family X members, including a single amino acid, H329A in Pol μ, that has a significant effect on template-independent synthesis but not on template-dependent synthesis during DNA end joining.

the structure of the polymerization domain of DNA polymerase μ in complex with DNA provides insight into the substrate preference of this polymerase, which is critical for nonhomologous end-joining of DNA.

Pol μ's substrate specificity is determined in part by the interactions of its active site with the incoming nucleotide and that these interactions are different from those in other family X polymerases.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the molecular basis of the substrate specificity and function of the DNA polymerase μ.
the molecular basis of the substrate specificity of Pol μ, and its role in DNA end joining.
the structure-function relationships of the family X DNA polymerase μ, a specialized enzyme involved in the nonhomologous end joining (N HEJ) of double stranded DNA breaks (DSB).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the structure of the polymerizing domain of Pol μ, in complex with a gapped DNA substrate and correct dNTP, reveals a number of interactions that are unique to this enzyme and provide a structural basis for its unusual substrate specificity.
the crystal structure of Pol μ bound to DNA with correct dNTP in the active site reveals a substrate specificity distinct from other family X DNA polymerase members.
the structural basis of Pol μ's unique substrate specificity is the presence of an arginine finger that is not present in Pol λ, Pol θ, or Pol κ.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Pol μ is a specialized polymerase that is able to carry out both template-dependent and -independent DNA synthesis, but it does not have the same substrate specificity as other family X members.
the crystal structure of the catalytic domain of DNA polymerase μ bound to DNA provides insight into the substrate preference of the enzyme and the basis for its unique role in DNA repair.
Pol μ's substrate specificity is determined by its active site, which has evolved to accommodate the unusual substrate requirements of NHEJ.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the structure of the DNA polymerase domain of Pol μ bound to a correct dNPTP substrate provides insights into the unusual substrate specificity and differing biological functions of Pol μ.
Pol μ has evolved a unique active site to accommodate its unusual NHEJ substrates.
Pol μ has evolved a unique set of amino acid residues in its active site that are critical for its specialized function in NHEJ.
